row.amal_said: عمي. / عمي. / My uncle or his uncle. Yes.
row.why: 'My uncle' is 3am + -i = 3ammi (sheet: uncle (paternal) | 3am | عم); he stuck -i onto 3ammo, a form that already carries its owner ending (Amal 12:30: 3ammo = my uncle or his uncle), so the fix is purely the possessive ending - grammar A4, not a vocab tier 2; Amal recast عمي at 12:21/12:24 and he took it ('That's right'); one row for the four uses (11:24, 11:37, 11:56, 12:18).

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same slip; the transcript supports grammar A4: the stem 3ammo is a word he knows and the only wrong thing is the stacked owner ending (-o + -i), which is the A4 rule, and the brief says an ending-rule fix is grammar, not tier 2.

row.chat: elyoam yoam el-jum3a talat 3ashara alafain u sitte u 3eshreen
row.why: Saying the date (13 = talat 3ashara, her chat) he said talat 3asha - the word for dinner (sheet: dinner | 3asha | عشا); this is not the engine (TR-26 el-3ashrah/el-3asha) because Amal reacted to it: she echoed عشاء at 15:42, he fixed to عشرة at 15:44, then she asked 'What's عشاء؟' and he said 'dinner'; tier 2 because it is a mangled form of a number he knows (sheet: ten | 3ashrah | عشرة), fixed the moment she echoed it, not a lexical choice of the wrong word.

rulings.why: Both readers keep it; tier 2 fits the transcript better than tier 1: he was producing a number he knows and dropped its last syllable into a sound-alike word, and he repaired it instantly on her echo (15:44, before her 15:45 question) - a wrong form of a known word, not a wrong-word choice. Her echo of his wrong form is a prompt, so the signal is prompt-then-fix.

row.why: In her 'شو يعني' drill Amal said الرحلة الأخيرة (35:23); repeating her phrase back before translating it he dropped el- from the adjective, which turns the phrase into the sentence 'the trip is last'; Amal recast الأخيرة and he said الرحلة الأخيرة (35:36). Listening mode: he was reproducing her Arabic in a comprehension drill, not building his own sentence; medium because the engine can drop a short el-, though Amal's recast shows she heard it missing.

rulings.why: Same slip, readers differ only on mode. The transcript shows a listening drill (she gives Arabic, he says what it means); his line is an echo of her phrase, so it belongs with the listening rows that are kept apart, as r2 ruled.

row.amal_said: حدا التاني is / no. X. Just حدا تاني.
row.why: Second try at 'someone else' after her 'تاني حدا would mean the second person' (43:18): he put el- on the adjective after the indefinite 7ada; Amal echoed حدا التاني and said 'no. X. Just حدا تاني' and he took it (43:45 حدا تاني). The engine wrote هذا الثاني; her echo gives what he said (trust Amal's echo). Filed A7 (where el- sits in noun + adjective) like the agreed A10/A20/A24 rows with el- on the adjective only; medium because his line is reconstructed from her echo.

rulings.why: Real and voiced: Amal's explicit 'no' and her echo prove the form even though the engine misheard his line. Not a duplicate of A27 (43:16 تاني حدا is a different wrong piece, this is his second, different attempt). Kept under A7 rather than PROPOSE because the el-on-adjective-only pattern is already filed A7 in this lesson's agreed rows.

row.why: For 'the last ten minutes' as noun + adjective he used the tool word aa5er (sheet: last / end | Aa5er | آخر) where the adjective a5eer is needed (sheet: last (adjective) | a5eer | أخير; the last... | El + noun + el + a5eer), the very distinction taught at 32:17; Amal prompted 'ال أخي-' at 45:58 and he switched to أخير، أخيرة. The wrong word choice is this row; the gender/plural slip that followed (46:06 أخير for أخيرات) is a separate fix and a separate row (D6). Her final form was الأخيرات (chat el-3ashar da2aaye2 el-a5eeraat).

rulings.why: Both readers saw a slip here; the transcript shows two fixes, not one: 45:58 she prompted him off the tool word آخر (a different sheet item, so vocab tier 1 as r1 wrote), and only at 46:10 did she fix the ending (D6). r2's combined grammar row is split into D5 + D6.

row.medi_said: الأخيرة. No، wait. دقيقة is, / is masculine. So، أخ-أخير.
row.why: He had reached الأخيرة, then called دقيقة masculine (it is feminine) and went back to masculine أخير; the plural feminine noun دقايق takes the plural adjective أخيرات - Amal recast it at 46:10 and he took it ('Oh, 'cause it's plural'). Separate from D5 (45:55 tool word آخر), which she had already fixed.

rulings.why: Real, voiced, and distinct from D5: a second fix on a second wrong piece (adjective agreement, A8) after he explicitly mis-gendered دقيقة. r2 folded it into the 45:55 row; the transcript shows two moments.

rulings.why: Plausibly real (two engine readings without b-, 39:04 and 1:04:01) but not provable: her line at the identical second is either a recast or her own goodbye. Kept with confidence low per the brief rather than dropped.
